data.heading: Where it started
data.description: Server images built from hand-written configuration, with environments drifting apart across deployment zones.

blocks.title: Business problem
blocks.body: Teams hand-wrote the configuration behind every server image, and each build took days. Environments drifted apart from one deployment zone to the next.

blocks.title: Technical barriers
blocks.body: Every image depended on someone reading the target software's official documentation and turning it into correct build configuration by hand.

blocks.title: Agivant's role
blocks.body: Multi-agent pipeline design, Config-as-Code generation, validation and security scanning, and pull-request automation

data.heading: What Agivant built
data.description: Agivant built a coordinated set of agents that takes each request from research through code generation, validation, build, and security scan. Two human approval gates sit after code generation and after scanning, and the finished image arrives as a pull request ready for sign-off. Value in days and weeks.

blocks.title: Documentation research
blocks.body: Reads the target software's official documentation and produces the exact steps needed to build its image.

blocks.title: Config-as-Code generation
blocks.body: Generates Packer and Terraform templates, so every build is declarative, idempotent, and repeatable.

blocks.title: Two-phase validation
blocks.body: Checks generated code for syntax, then re-validates it against a documentation-derived checklist, looping back on any gap.

blocks.title: Build and security scan
blocks.body: Builds the immutable image with Packer and runs a Trivy vulnerability scan, retrying automatically when a build fails.

blocks.title: Pull-request automation
blocks.body: Opens a pull request with an auto-populated review checklist in GitHub or Stash, ready for human sign-off.

blocks.title: Observability and cost tracking
blocks.body: Langfuse tracks agent performance and per-model cost for every image the pipeline produces.

rows.label: Controls
rows.value: Two human approval gates, after code generation and after scanning

blocks.title: Before
blocks.body: Hand-written configuration, days per image, and environment drift across deployment zones.

blocks.title: After
blocks.body: One request producing validated Packer and Terraform templates, an immutable build, a Trivy scan, and a review-ready pull request.

data.heading: Proof in production
data.description: In a demonstration run, one plain-English request for a Langflow image went through research, code generation, validation, build, and a clean security scan, ending in an auto-created pull request. Every stage streamed live, with human approval gates along the way, and the image was built in minutes.

blocks.heading: Measured results
blocks.description: A production-ready image, minted and shipped from one request.

blocks.label: Image build time in the demonstration run
Human approval gates on every image

blocks.title: Reusable asset
blocks.body: Declarative Packer and Terraform templates hold environment parity across every deployment zone and cloud target, so images stay standard across clouds and teams. Every build amplifies the next.

blocks.title: Challenges overcome
blocks.body: Making sure only correct configuration reaches the build stage, recovering from failed builds automatically, and keeping an autonomous pipeline fully auditable through human gates.
